Shameless Sega kiddie here. The 32x was one of those "Brilliant concept, but utterly stupid" things. It was a true retrofit to a pre existing piece of consumer hardware, and it did it's job well, but it was needless. We had the Saturn right around the corner, the nomad was on the market, the Genny and it's cd system still being supported, and competing systems from Sony, Nintendo and Atari. Most of us thought the thing was odd, even back then. Still, it did deliver the goods, when it was in the hands of programmers who gave a damn. It's port of Space Harrier was pretty much arcade-exact, Shadow squadron was fucking tight, Kolibri was excellent, Knuckles chaotix really showed what the tech could do (it's soundtrack was fucking legit). Virtua racing deluxe is still fun.
